title: Why your review queue feels shorter than it looks
excerpt: The SM-2 algorithm behind your reviews doesn't just track whether you got a word right — it tracks how easy it felt. A word you struggle with resets its interval, but one you find easy stretches out fast, sometimes to months between reviews. That's why a deck of 200 words rarely means 200 reviews a day.

title: The untranslatable words hiding in your target language
excerpt: Every language carries a handful of words with no clean equivalent elsewhere — the Portuguese saudade, the Russian тоска, the Tajik армон. Learning to recognize these isn't a detour from grammar and vocabulary; it's often the fastest way into how native speakers actually think.

title: Reading above your level is not a mistake
excerpt: Stories in Glossa are tagged by CEFR level, but reaching slightly above your current level — with a story's built-in translations and clickable vocabulary — is a well-documented way to absorb grammar patterns before you can consciously explain them.

title: Why a broken streak matters less than you think
excerpt: Streak counters reward consistency, but the underlying spaced-repetition schedule doesn't punish a missed day the way a game score would — a card due yesterday is still due today. Missing one day resets your streak counter, not your progress.
